# Jubilees Chapter 36 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QJub (Hebrew fragments) | **Section:** Isaac's final words; dividing the inheritance; Isaac dies

---

**36:1** In the forty-fifth jubilee, seventh week, first year, Isaac called Esau and Jacob to him. Both sons came.

**36:2** "Sons," he said, "I'm dying. Today I'm settling my affairs — dividing what I have between the two of you.

**36:3** Listen carefully to what I say. Do it. Your lives may depend on it.

**36:4** Honor your mother — she gave birth to both of you. And love each other. Don't nurse contempt in your hearts.

**36:5** Love your brother. Don't carry hostility. Don't become the kind of brothers who hate each other.

**36:6** Don't let Mastema's spirit take hold of you or your children. Don't let him drag you toward destruction.

**36:7** I know Esau has been jealous and angry about the blessing I gave you, Jacob. But I am commanding him right now: do not harm Jacob."

**36:8** He turned to Esau: "I'm old, Esau. My eyes are gone and I have no strength left.

**36:9** You've seen what I gave Jacob. Yes, he received more. But I have given you plenty too. You both have an inheritance from me.

**36:10** Your place is in the mountains of Seir — go there and rule it. From the eastern frontier to all the borders of Edom, that's yours. Jacob gets Canaan — everything from the great river to the sea.

**36:11** Don't move against Jacob. Don't try to take what's his. Love him — fully, completely — and live in peace with him.

**36:12** If he serves you well and with a good heart, don't make it hard for him — he's your brother. If he serves you faithfully, that's good. But if I hear that you have been treacherous — I will curse you with my last breath."

**36:13** Esau said: "I'll do everything you've said. I won't move against Jacob. He is my brother."

**36:14** Isaac was genuinely moved. He blessed Esau: "May the LORD God of Israel bless you, prosper your path, multiply your children, and let your family possess everything your heart could wish for."

**36:15** Then he blessed Jacob: "Jacob, the son I love — may God bless you from above with heaven's dew and earth's richness.

**36:16** May God Almighty bless you and make your path successful, and may your family grow great and multiply."

**36:17** Then he gathered them both again and made his formal declaration. He assigned the whole land of Canaan to Jacob and the Seir highlands to Esau.

**36:18** "I give the entire land of Canaan to Jacob and to his children forever. Seir — all of it — belongs to Esau."

**36:19** Isaac died. Jacob and Esau buried him at Mamre in the cave at Machpelah, where their grandfather Abraham lay.

**36:20** Both sons wept deeply, and the whole household mourned with them.

---

*PNEUMA notes: Isaac's testament formally divides the world between the two sons — Canaan for Israel, Seir for Edom. This is Jubilees' theological resolution of the Israel-Edom conflict: both receive a legitimate inheritance but in separate territories. The warning against Mastema (v.6) shows how Jubilees frames interpersonal conflict as supernatural warfare.*
